summary: A 1933 BC-201 lookout-fireman cabin on Mendocino NF with a 180-degree view, used as a WWII aircraft warning post and now restored and rentable.

facts.design: BC-201 lookout-fireman cabin, windows on three sides, 180-degree viewing area

access.note: Restored and in the Forest Service rental program; reached by car through a combination-locked gate, May through October.

visit.trail_note: Accessible by car when the rental season is open; group size capped at six, no overnight camping elsewhere on site.

events.note: Built as a BC-201 lookout-fireman cabin on the Mendocino National Forest.
Recreation.gov states regular fire-detection use ran until 1942, though staffing accounts below extend past this date.
Mr. and Mrs. B.M. Bucknell took over as lookouts, replacing Ralph Johnson after he was injured.
Earl Mersinger was injured fighting fire near the lookout; Mrs. Carl Capell and niece June Marie Bauer took over staffing.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, April 20, 2009 (per brief/NHLR record).

evidence.supports: Built 1933 as BC-201 cabin with 180-degree view; WWII aircraft warning use; restored and in rental system.
evidence.quote: Built on the Mendocino National Forest in 1933, Pine Mountain Lookout is a BC-201 lookout-fireman cabin with windows on three sides covering a 180 degree viewing area. In World War II it was an aircraft warning station. Recently restored, it is now in the rental system.

evidence.supports: Constructed 1933, used for fire detection until 1942, WWII aircraft defense monitoring, notable for 180-degree view.
evidence.quote: Rustic Pine Mountain Lookout was constructed in 1933 and used for fire detection until 1942. During World War II, the lookout served as part of an aircraft defense monitoring system that extended throughout California.

evidence.supports: Open May through October, accessible by car.
evidence.quote: The lookout is typically open from May through October and is accessible by car.

evidence.supports: Gate combination and group size/camping rules.
evidence.quote: Pine Mountain Lookout is accessed through a gate with a combination lock. The combination is included in your email conformation.

evidence.supports: 1943 staffing by the Bucknells, replacing injured Ralph Johnson.
evidence.quote: Thursday morning Mr. and Mrs. B.M. Bucknell took their posts at the Pine Mountain forestry lookout for the summer months, replacing Ralph Johnson, who was recently injured and unable to carry on the work at Pine Mountain.

evidence.supports: 1944 staffing change after Earl Mersinger's injury fighting fire near Pine Mountain.
evidence.quote: Earl Mersinger, who was hurt about two weeks ago on Pine mountain while fire fighting, will be in Howard Memorial Hospital, Willits, for some time due to a foot injury... Mr. Mersinger is forestry lookout at Pine Mountain, near Upper Lake.

evidence.supports: Mrs. Carl Capell and niece June Marie Bauer took over staffing after Mersinger's injury.
evidence.quote: The Mersingers have been stationed on the Pine Hill Lookout in Lake county, but after Mr. Mersinger's injury the position was taken by Mrs. Carl Capell. June Marie Bauer is also at the lookout, assisting her aunt.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Recreation.gov says fire detection ran only until 1942, but newspaper accounts from the weebly site document lookout staffing in 1943 and 1944 at this same site (same Bucknell Creek/Upper Lake area). The story notes this discrepancy rather than picking one date.

sources.title: Pine Mountain Lookout, Mendocino National Forest

notes_for_editor: Brief's 2009 NHLR registration date and firelookout.org county label ('Los Angeles') for NHLR US 773 appear to be a rendering glitch on the firelookout.org list page; NHLR's own detail page confirms Mendocino NF, so I did not use firelookout.org as a cited source. Did not independently verify the 2009 registration date against a primary NHLR page excerpt (the live NHLR page I fetched didn't show the registration date field in the text returned), so it's carried from the brief rather than newly confirmed. Verification pass 2026-10-04: re-fetched californialookouts.weebly.com directly and confirmed via the Aug 7, 1944 Redwood Journal item that Mersinger's injury happened 'on Pine mountain while fire fighting' and that he is 'forestry lookout at Pine Mountain, near Upper Lake' -- the separate Aug 9, 1944 Ukiah Republican Press item calls the site the 'Pine Hill Lookout,' which is an inconsistency in the original press clippings, not a different site; both articles are about the same lookout and both are now cited.
